inputs.sbc_source: Annual Report FY2025 and Interim Report H1 FY2026: no share option or share award scheme, no share-based payment add-back in the cash flow statement (SBC-zero market); EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. fx_rate is CNY->HKD 1.1747 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-22; inverse HKDCNY=X 0.8504 ties to 1/1.1747 = 0.8513). No dual listing for a parity check; loose cross-check: the FY2025 final dividend of HK$0.20/share was booked as RMB743.5m dividends payable at 30 June 2026 (HKD/CNY 0.8686 at the declaration date), the same direction and within the period's FX drift. Per-share values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD; unsuffixed intrinsic_value/weighted_iv are HKD so they compare to current_price.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-22T08:08:33Z (HKEX regular-session close 16:08 HKT; not an after-hours print)
inputs.share_count_basis: 4,280,100,000 ordinary shares of HK$0.10 (Interim Report H1 FY2026 note 8); unchanged since FY2017; no options, awards or convertibles, so basic = fully diluted. Held flat: no SBC to charge and no issuance pending.
inputs.net_cash_composition: At 30 June 2026 (Interim Report note 15, RMB m): cash and cash equivalents 3,724.2 + time deposits with original maturity >3 months 3,552.5 (current 3,092.8 + non-current 459.7) = 7,276.6 cash-like; interest-bearing bank borrowings nil (RMB20.0m at FY2025 repaid). EXCLUDED from cash: pledged deposits 457.3 (collateral for bank acceptance bills payable, i.e. operating), and the FVTPL portfolio (wealth-management products 693.1 + listed equities held for trading 207.7 = 900.8) which is carried separately in equity_bridge so that its stripped income has its matching asset. The RMB743.5m FY2025 final dividend (HK$0.20/share, paid 31 July 2026) was a liability at the balance-sheet date and the price is ex-dividend, so it is deducted in equity_bridge.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10y CGB ~1.8% risk-free + China equity risk premium ~6.5% x beta ~1.2 for a domestic-cycle machinery maker = ~9.6%; rounded to 9.5%. Capital structure is all-equity (zero borrowings, RMB7.3bn cash) so WACC = cost of equity. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality, trade-remedy risk and the family-controlled cash pile are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: None required. Right-of-use assets (RMB111.7m) are predominantly PRC land-use rights with no lease liability on the face of the balance sheet; no lease-liability line, lease principal immaterial. Lease amortisation sits inside D&A and no lease liability is in net debt, so leases are charged once, through the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests RMB2.8m (0.02% of equity, RMB0.1m of H1 FY2026 profit). Flows are consolidated; the NCI stock is deducted once in equity_bridge for completeness. Immaterial either way.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-US and cyclical, so owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md applied). Why: a construction-machinery manufacturer whose value is a stream of free cash flow plus a very large net-cash position. Owner FCF FY2025 = reported FCF 1,183.0 (OCF 1,244.6 - capex 61.5) - SBC 0 - finance income 147.9 = 1,035.1 (RMB m). Finance income is stripped because net cash (~RMB7.4bn including FVTPL and after the dividend) is ~7x the FCF base; its source assets are added in the bridge at face. The EBITDA margin path is anchored to an OPERATING EBITDA that also excludes the FY2025 'other gains and losses' investment items (FVTPL fair-value gains 104.7, FVTPL disposal gains 3.0, FVTPL dividends 7.4, derivative losses -22.2; note 5), which gives 13.6% for FY2025 and ~12.5% for FY2024 against the 14.4%/13.2% that the Metrics EBITDA line shows -- matching-asset rule. Working capital: a manufacturer with receivables + inventory well above payables (net operating WC ~RMB1.2bn, ~10% of annualised revenue, and FY2025/H1 FY2026 receivables growing faster than sales on extended terms for electric machines), so wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE (-12%): growth consumes cash and a downturn releases it. Capex (0.5% of revenue FY2025, 1.1% H1 FY2026) has run far below D&A (2.1%) for four years; the paths converge capex up to 1.8% and D&A down to 1.8% so the terminal year is not capitalising under-investment. Cash tax: the FY2025 cash rate of 8.4% is a timing low (P&L rate 14.8%; High-and-New-Technology Enterprise 15% rate plus PRC dividend withholding), so the cash rate starts at 16% and drifts to 18%. SBC-zero: house and street coincide, band_position is null. SANITY-CHECK FIX 2026-10-22 (growth_too_high): base 10-year revenue CAGR capped at the FY2017-FY2025 through-cycle CAGR of 2.8% (was 4.7%); terminal values capped at the stock's own 10-year EV/EBITDA range -- bear 3.7x (10yr min), base 6.6x (10yr average), bull 10.9x (10yr max) -- translated into the engine's owner-FCF cap multiples via each scenario's terminal EBITDA/FCF ratio (~1.51 / ~1.43 / ~1.42): bear 5.6x, base 9.5x, bull 14x (the bull translation is ~15.5x, looser than the 14x already judged, so 14x is kept as the tighter of the two). At 9.5% WACC Gordon is 13.6x (g 2.0%) / 15.9x (g 3.0%), so the cap binds in every scenario. FY0 = FY2025; Y1 = FY2026, the guidance year, which is three-quarters elapsed (H1 FY2026 revenue +19.0%, net profit +22.4%).

equity_bridge.item: Financial assets at FVTPL: wealth-management products 693.1 + listed equities held for trading 207.7, at fair value
equity_bridge.note: Interim Report H1 FY2026 note 14, 30 June 2026. Their fair-value gains and dividends are excluded from the operating EBITDA anchor, so the asset enters the bridge at face (matching-asset rule).

equity_bridge.item: FY2025 final dividend HK$0.20/share, declared at 28 May 2026 AGM, payable at 30 June 2026, paid 31 July 2026
equity_bridge.note: Interim Report H1 FY2026 balance sheet 'Dividends payable'. Cash had not yet left at the balance-sheet date; the quoted price is ex-dividend.
Interim Report H1 FY2026 balance sheet; consolidated flows, NCI deducted once here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR (FY2025 -> FY2035) of 2.77%, capped at the through-cycle revenue CAGR FY2017 -> FY2025 of 2.797% (first to last year of available data: RMB8,994m -> RMB11,215m over 8 years) per the sanity-check runbook growth_too_high fix. Recorded as the path's own CAGR rather than a rounded 2.8 so it reads inside, not above, the cap. Sits inside the 2.6-5.6% equity-CAGR bracket. Front-loaded by the current up-cycle (H1 FY2026 +19%), decelerating to 1% by FY2032 and 2.0% terminal. Prior to the fix the selected rate was 4.7%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR +2.6% vs revenue -2.7% and EPS -8.2%: the FY2020 base year was the last cycle peak (revenue RMB12.9bn, EPS RMB0.46) and FY2022 the trough (EPS RMB0.09), so every 3- and 5-year CAGR here is a cycle artefact. 3yr EPS +49% off the trough and 3yr FCF -12% off a working-capital-release year are equally unrepresentative. The FY2017-FY2025 through-cycle revenue CAGR (2.8%, spanning a full peak and trough) and the equity CAGR (dividend-dampened, ~2.6-5.6%) are the only usable long-run signals.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less finance income; SBC is zero throughout): FY2020 632.8, FY2022 1,499.8, FY2025 1,035.1 (RMB m). Owner-FCF CAGRs track reported FCF CAGRs within 2pp because finance income is a stable ~RMB120-165m a year; the gap between the two series is the level, not the growth. Reported FCF is dominated by working-capital swings (FY2021 37, FY2022 1,617, FY2023 1,798) so no single-period CAGR is a forecast anchor.

base.growth_rationale: 10-year CAGR 2.77%, capped at the FY2017-FY2025 through-cycle revenue CAGR of 2.8% (sanity-check growth_too_high fix; the prior path was 15/8/5/3/3/3/3/2.5/2.5/2.5 = 4.7%). FY2026 +15% is kept because it is largely banked: H1 +19.0% on a domestic equipment-renewal surge and exports +21%, with tougher H2 comps (H2 FY2025 was RMB5.6bn) and a CCMA industry run-rate already decelerating from the >20% of mid-2026. The cap is absorbed from FY2027: +3%/+2% as the renewal cycle matures and forklifts keep shrinking, 1.5% through FY2031 and 1% thereafter, i.e. a through-cycle view in which the next downturn is averaged into the path rather than modelled as a discrete event (that is the bear case). Terminal growth 2.0%, below the prior 2.5%, consistent with the 1% end-of-path rate.
base.margin_rationale: Operating EBITDA (ex finance income and ex FVTPL/derivative gains) was 12.5% FY2024, 13.6% FY2025, ~13.4% H1 FY2026. 13.75% in the up-cycle years, fading to 13.0% mid-cycle as the forklift price war and steel costs offset the excavator/export mix gain. The 9-year average of the Metrics EBITDA margin is 13.8% including investment gains; peak was 19.5% (FY2020), trough 5.5% (FY2022). Unchanged by the growth fix: the margin anchor is the last two reported years, not the growth path.
base.terminal_cap_rationale: 9.5x terminal owner FCF = the stock's 10-year average EV/EBITDA of 6.6x (sanity_check historical_averages_ex_outliers, FY2017-FY2025) x terminal EBITDA/FCF ~1.43 (EBITDA 13.0%, D&A = capex 1.8%, cash tax 18%, WC drag 0.12% of revenue at 1% growth). Was 12x FCF (~8.2x EBITDA). Binding: Gordon at 9.5%/2.0% is 13.6x.

bull.growth_rationale: 10-year CAGR 5.0% (trimmed from 6.4% alongside the base-case cap so the scenario ordering stays coherent: bull = through-cycle 2.8% plus ~2pp of export and mix gain). Exports keep compounding high-teens for two more years (record RMB3.8bn FY2025, +21% H1 FY2026) without new trade remedies beyond the UK excavator duties; excavators (+60% FY2025, +28% H1 FY2026) and electric loaders lift the domestic franchise through the 15th Five-Year Plan; forklift electrification arrests that segment's decline.
bull.margin_rationale: Mix shift to excavators/exports plus gross-margin expansion (19.6% -> 21.4% -> 21.55%) carries operating EBITDA to 15.5%, still well below the 18-19.5% of FY2019-20, which required a domestic super-cycle. Unchanged by the fix.
bull.terminal_cap_rationale: The runbook's bull cap is the 10-year maximum EV/EBITDA of 10.9x, which at a terminal EBITDA/FCF of ~1.42 is ~15.5x FCF -- looser than the 14x FCF (~9.9x EBITDA) already judged for a sub-scale Chinese cyclical, so 14x is retained as the tighter of the two. Binding: Gordon at 9.5%/3.0% is 15.9x.

bear.growth_rationale: Unchanged by the fix (10-year CAGR ~-0.1%, already below the through-cycle 2.8%). FY2026 still finishes +10% on the H1 already banked, then the 2022-23 pattern repeats: domestic old-for-new subsidies fade, property/infrastructure investment disappoints again, and trade-remedy actions spread from the UK to other export markets, so revenue falls ~19% over FY2027-29 (FY2021-23 was -23%) before a 2% crawl. Revenue in FY2035 is roughly flat on FY2025.
bear.margin_rationale: Operating EBITDA margin troughs at 8% (FY2022 trough was 5.5% on the Metrics basis) under forklift and loader price competition, and recovers only to 11%, two points below mid-cycle, as the scale gap to XCMG/SANY/Zoomlion compounds. Working capital releases cash in the down years (negative capture on a falling revenue delta), which is why owner FCF does not collapse with EBITDA. Unchanged by the fix.
bear.terminal_cap_rationale: 5.6x terminal owner FCF = the stock's 10-year minimum EV/EBITDA of 3.7x (FY2023, the last trough) x terminal EBITDA/FCF ~1.51 (EBITDA 11%, D&A = capex 1.8%, cash tax 18%, WC drag 0.24% at 2% growth). Was 10x FCF (~6.6x EBITDA). This is the market's trough pricing of the operating business, i.e. the bear case assumes the operating franchise never re-rates off its cyclical low.

scenario_narratives.base: China's construction-machinery recovery that began in 2025 runs through FY2026 (revenue +15%, H1 already +19%) and then the path reverts to the FY2017-FY2025 through-cycle growth rate of 2.8% a year, compounded over ten years: domestic equipment renewal and 15th Five-Year Plan infrastructure keep loaders and excavators growing while forklifts keep shrinking under price competition, exports (34% of FY2025 sales) grow faster than the group but face incremental trade friction, and the next downturn is averaged into the path rather than modelled as an event. Operating EBITDA margin holds ~13.75% while volumes are rising and settles at 13% mid-cycle; capex normalises back toward D&A after four years of under-investment; working capital absorbs ~12% of each year's revenue increase as electric machines sell on extended terms. Terminal value is capped at the stock's own 10-year average EV/EBITDA of 6.6x (9.5x owner FCF), so the base case assumes NO re-rating of the operating business relative to its own history; the upside to the price is the net cash credited at face plus the operating franchise at its historical multiple.
scenario_narratives.bull: Chinese machinery brands keep taking global share: Lonking's exports compound high-teens for two more years along Belt and Road and resource-rich emerging markets without new anti-dumping actions, excavators and electric loaders keep lifting mix, and forklift electrification turns that segment from drag to contributor, for a 10-year revenue CAGR of 5% (through-cycle plus ~2pp). Gross margin keeps expanding (19.6% -> 21.4% -> 21.55% and on) so operating EBITDA reaches 15.5%; the board keeps lifting the payout (58% in FY2025) and the market starts to credit the cash pile. Exit at 14x owner FCF (~9.9x EBITDA), below the stock's own 10-year maximum of 10.9x and well short of the FY2019-20 margin peak.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 'bottoming recovery' management describes proves to be a subsidy-driven renewal spike rather than a new up-cycle. From FY2027 domestic volumes roll over as old-for-new incentives fade and property/infrastructure investment disappoints, while trade remedies spread from the UK's 18.8-83.5% excavator duties to other developed and emerging markets, stalling the export engine. Revenue falls ~19% over three years (FY2021-23 was -23%), operating EBITDA margin troughs at 8% in a loader/forklift price war, and receivables stretched on electric machines produce credit losses. The cash pile cushions the equity but the operating business exits at the stock's own 10-year trough multiple of 3.7x EV/EBITDA (5.6x owner FCF): a sub-scale player (vs XCMG/SANY/Zoomlion) whose cash the family-controlled board returns only partially, and which the market never re-rates.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: this is a high-cyclicality business two-thirds exposed to China property/infrastructure investment that fell 23% peak-to-trough last cycle, whose growth engine (exports) is now the explicit target of trade-remedy actions, and whose net cash (over 70% of market cap) is controlled by a 57% family holder, so the market may never pay for it in full. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold at once: exports untouched by further protectionism, a durable domestic up-cycle, and a margin re-rate to 15.5%. Base 50%. Weights unchanged by the sanity-check fix; the fix moved the paths and the exit multiples, not the odds.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Lonking is valued as two things: a net-cash-and-investments position and a cyclical, sub-scale but consistently profitable loader/forklift/excavator franchise generating ~RMB1.0-1.2bn of owner FCF a year at mid-cycle. The DCF strips finance income and investment gains from the flows and puts their source assets in the bridge at face, so the cash is counted exactly once. The growth path is capped at the through-cycle rate and the exit multiples at the stock's own trading history, so the base case does not require the market to pay more for the operating business than it has on average over the last decade; what it does require is that the cash be credited at face.
valuation_philosophy.re_rate_free_floor: At 30 June 2026 the group held RMB7,276.6m of cash and time deposits with zero borrowings (71% of the market capitalisation of ~RMB10.2bn at current_price and CNY/HKD 1.1747), plus RMB900.8m of FVTPL wealth-management products and listed equities (80% of market cap together). Net of the RMB743.5m FY2025 final dividend that was still a liability at that date and was paid on 31 July 2026 (the price is ex-dividend), the position is RMB7,433m = RMB1.74 = HK$2.04 per share, 73% of the share price. That is the re-rate-free floor: the ~HK$0.75 the market pays above it buys ~RMB1.0bn a year of owner FCF at under 3x, i.e. the market capitalises the operating franchise near its FY2023 trough multiple and treats most of the cash as trapped inside PRC subsidiaries under a 57% family holder. The house view credits the cash at face (payout was 58% in FY2025, so it is being returned, if slowly) and charges the cyclicality and governance risk through a 25% bear weight and historical-range exit multiples rather than through an ad-hoc discount on the cash.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_fix: The first build (base IV HK$6.54, +134% at a price in the upper 77% of its 10-year range) tripped scripts/sanity_check.py with diagnosis growth_too_high: the base 10-year revenue CAGR of 4.7% exceeded the FY2017-FY2025 through-cycle CAGR of 2.8%. Fix applied per the runbook (Step 8c.5, items 3 and 4): (1) base growth path capped at a 2.77% 10-year CAGR, keeping the banked FY2026 +15% and flattening to 1% by FY2032, terminal growth 2.5% -> 2.0%; bull trimmed 6.4% -> 5.0% for ordering; bear unchanged (~0%). (2) Exit-multiple caps set from the stock's own 10-year EV/EBITDA range -- bear 3.7x (min), base 6.6x (average), bull 10.9x (max) -- expressed as owner-FCF cap multiples of 5.6x / 9.5x / 14x (bull kept at the tighter 14x already judged). Margins, capex, D&A, tax, working capital, WACC, bridge and weights were deliberately left unchanged: none of them was the diagnosed cause and the margin anchor is reported history, not the growth path. The residual upside after the fix is almost entirely the cash: the 10-year historical multiples the check compares against were struck on an EV that had already deducted the cash, so a model that credits the cash at face will always print a higher P/B and EV/EBITDA than the stock's own history. Whether that credit is deserved is the governance risk, not a growth or multiple error.
key_risks_to_valuation: Trapped-cash discount: ~HK$2.04/share of the value (73% of the price) is cash, time deposits and wealth-management products inside PRC subsidiaries under a 57% family holder; a 58% payout returns some of it, but a buyer of the shares cannot compel its return and the market has historically capitalised it at a steep discount -- this, not growth or the exit multiple, is what the residual upside after the sanity-check fix turns on
China construction cycle: domestic sales (~66%) fell 23% across FY2021-23; the current recovery is subsidy- and renewal-driven and the bear case assumes it repeats
Trade remedies on exports: the UK's 18.8-83.5% anti-dumping duties on Chinese excavators (May 2025) are the template; exports are the only structural growth driver

Receivables quality: trade and long-term receivables are growing faster than revenue on extended terms for electric machines (long-term receivables +82% in H1 FY2026); a downturn converts that into credit losses that the model's -12% WC capture does not fully price
Forklift segment (25-31% of revenue) is shrinking in both volume and price; a faster decline than assumed takes the mid-cycle margin below 13%
FX: RMB flows against an HKD quote; the fx_rate 1.1747 is dated 2026-10-22 and is not refreshed by price-only updates
Capex has run at a quarter of D&A for four years; if the 'technology deployment reform' and electrification require a step-up beyond the 1.8% of revenue modelled, FCF conversion falls

Through-cycle cap is itself a judgment: FY2017 (start of the measured CAGR) was mid-recovery, not a trough, so 2.8% is not obviously conservative; a FY2016 trough start would read higher and a FY2020 peak start lower

implied_multiples_after_fix.script_basis_note: As printed by scripts/sanity_check.py at base IV (SBC-adjusted basis, SBC is nil here). These run ~1.17x above the hand-converted figures on P/E, P/B and P/S and further above on EV/EBITDA, consistent with the known CNY/HKD fx-direction issue in sanity_check.py (memory: sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-systemic-bug); the hand-converted multiples below are the ones to read.
implied_multiples_after_fix.hand_converted_note: FY2025 net income RMB1,300.5m, equity RMB11,479.3m, Metrics EBITDA RMB1,620.5m (operating EBITDA ex investment gains ~RMB1,525m), revenue RMB11,215.2m; EV = equity value less cash 7,276.6 less FVTPL 900.8 plus the 743.5 dividend liability.
implied_multiples_after_fix.verdict: Materially improved, not a pass: base upside 134% -> 103% against the same upside-vs-10yr-range rule (price at 77% of range). The growth and terminal-multiple candidates are now exhausted -- the base terminal sits at the 10yr average EV/EBITDA and the bear at the 10yr minimum, and the FY2025 multiples at base IV (P/E 15.9x, EV/EBITDA 8.2x) are inside the stock's own 10yr range (max 20.1x / 10.9x). The residual gap is the RMB7.4bn of net cash and investments (73% of market cap, HK$2.04/share) that the model credits at face and the market has historically capitalised at a steep discount; that is a governance judgment carried in the 25% bear weight, not a growth or multiple error, so per the runbook this is one fix pass and it is not iterated further.
